Gli adenocarcinomi della giunzione esofa:
Adenocarcinomas of the gastroesophageal junction on CT appear as asymmetric wall thickening or a mass extending upward along the distal esophagus and downward into the cardia and fundus. According to the AJCC 8th edition, tumors with an epicenter within 2 cm below the junction are staged as esophageal, those with an epicenter lower down as gastric; the exact site is defined by endoscopy.

Pitfalls: a poorly distended stomach makes the cardia wall look thick (here, however, the thickness of about 3.5 cm and the mass-like appearance are unequivocal: to study the stomach it is better to distend it with water); do not confuse fundal varices with solid tissue; do not forget the liver, lymph nodes (paracardial, lesser curvature, celiac trunk), peritoneum and, in women, the ovaries. CT does not see small carcinomatosis: in surgical candidates staging laparoscopy is performed; T is better assessed with endoscopic ultrasound and PET-CT helps in the search for distant metastases.

In this case the patient had metastatic disease: the collection data report a liver biopsy of metastatic disease in addition to the primary tumor tissue.
Ispessimento asimmetrico e a massa della: Asymmetric, mass-like thickening of the gastroesophageal junction and cardia: neoplasm until proven otherwise; always look for liver metastases, lymph nodes and carcinomatosis.
